scientificStatementCalibration.formerStatement: Local SHA-256 và byte count cung cấp 100% mathematical proof of archive integrity
scientificStatementCalibration.calibratedStatement: Local artifact integrity và transport completeness đã được xác minh; upstream identity chưa thể kiểm chứng độc lập do nguồn không công bố checksum chuẩn.
scientificStatementCalibration.calibrationRationale: A local SHA-256 proves bit-level immutability of the artifact currently in possession, but cannot prove equivalence to the author's original canonical release without an authoritative, independently published upstream cryptographic hash.

tierA_local_artifact_integrity.measurementMethod: Live SHA-256 computation over local tar.gz files and exact byte count matching against download-receipt.json.
tierA_local_artifact_integrity.conclusion: No post-acquisition bit rot or modifications detected across all 4 archives.

tierB_transport_completeness.measurementMethod: Content-Length header verification, safe extraction without error, and PIL image decoding.

criteria.imageDecodeRate: 100.0% (6,156 uncompressed images successfully decoded via PIL)
criteria.fileCountAndPairabilityMatch: 684 unique instances match exactly across orig and sd2-sp with 1:1 and 1:6 paired mappings

tierB_transport_completeness.conclusion: Transport was complete; no corruption occurred during transfer or extraction.

tierC_upstream_identity.measurementMethod: Review of upstream TGIF paper, project repository, and server share for published authoritative hashes.
tierC_upstream_identity.findings: Upstream TGIF maintainers published files on a Nextcloud public share without publishing an authoritative SHA-256 or MD5 manifest. Therefore, while our local copy is verified complete and unaltered since acquisition, third-party cryptographic proof that our archive is byte-for-byte identical to the original release at t=0 remains unavailable until upstream publishes a signature or hash ledger.
tierC_upstream_identity.recommendation: Maintain persistent acquisition bindings, receipts, and reproduction scripts so any third party can verify against the identical Nextcloud files.
